paragraphs: Seneca Foods Corporation ("Seneca" or the "Company") was founded in 1949 and has evolved through internal growth and strategic acquisitions into a leading provider of packaged fruits and vegetables, with 27 main facilities located throughout the United States. The facilities are comprised of plants for packaging, can manufacturing, seed production, a farming operation and a logistical support network. Food packaging operations are primarily supported by plant locations in New York, Michigan, Oregon, Wisconsin, Washington, Idaho, Illinois, Minnesota, and Arizona. The Company also maintains warehouses which are generally located adjacent to its packaging plants. The Company is incorporated in New York with its headquarters located at 350 WillowBrook Office Park, Fairport, New York 14450 and its telephone number is (585) 495-4100.

The Company's business strategies are designed to grow its market share and enhance sales and margins. These strategies include: 1) expand the Company's leadership in the packaged fruit and vegetable industry; 2) provide low-cost, high-quality fruit and vegetable products to consumers through the elimination of costs from the Company's supply chain and investment in state-of-the-art production and logistical technology; 3) invest in growth opportunities; and 4) pursue strategic acquisitions that leverage the Company's core competencies.

The Company's Internet address is www.senecafoods.com. The Company's annual report on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K and any amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, are available on the Company's website, as soon as reasonably practicable after they are electronically filed with or furnished to the SEC. All such filings on the Company's website are available free of charge. Information on our website is not part of the annual report on Form 10-K.

In addition, the Company's website includes items related to corporate governance matters, including charters of various committees of the Board of Directors and the Company's Code of Business Conduct and Ethics. The Company intends to disclose on its website any amendment to or waiver of any provision of the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics that would otherwise be required to be disclosed under the rules of the SEC and NASDAQ.

The Company manages its business almost entirely on the basis of two reportable food packaging segments: Vegetable and Fruit/Snack. The Other category comprises non-food operations including revenue derived from the sale of cans, ends, seed, and outside revenue from the Company's aircraft operations, and certain corporate items. During fiscal 2026, the Company acquired the Green Giant U.S. frozen business which is part of the vegetable reportable segment. This acquisition enhances the Company's existing frozen capabilities and expands its reach in the frozen category. Refer to the information set forth under the heading "Acquisition" in Note 16 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item 8, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data", for additional details.

The Company's food operations constituted 98% of total net sales in fiscal year 2026. Canned vegetables represented 82%, frozen vegetables represented 9%, fruit products represented 6%, and snack products represented 1% of the total food packaging net sales. Non-food packaging sales represented 2% of the Company's fiscal year 2026 net sales. Refer to the information set forth under the heading "Segment Information" in Note 13 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item 8, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data", for additional discussion about the Company's segments.
The Company's principal product offerings include canned, frozen and jarred fruits and vegetables, as well as packaged snack chips. The Company manufactures and sells the following:

private label products are sold nationwide by major grocery outlets, such as supermarkets, mass merchandisers, limited assortment stores, club stores and dollar stores, for resale under the retailers' own or controlled labels;

private label and branded products to the foodservice industry, including foodservice distributors and national restaurant operators, in addition to products sold to federal, state and local governments for school and other food programs;
branded products under national and regional brands that the Company owns or licenses, including Aunt Nellie's®, CherryMan®, Green Giant®, Green Valley®, Libby's®, READ® and Seneca®;
branded products under co-pack agreements to other major branded companies for their distribution;
products to the Company's industrial customer base for use as ingredients by other food manufacturers; and
products to export customers in approximately 55 countries.

headings: Fruit and Vegetable Industry Risks
Excess capacity in the fruit and vegetable industry has a downward impact on selling price.
Growing cycles and adverse weather conditions may decrease our results from operations.
The commodity materials that we package or otherwise require are subject to price increases that could adversely affect our profitability.
Risks Associated with Our Operations
Changes in economic conditions that impact consumer spending could harm our business.
We depend upon key customers.
If we do not maintain the market shares of our products, our business and revenues may be adversely affected.
Increases in logistics and other transportation-related costs could materially adversely impact our results of operations.

A recall of our products could have a material adverse effect on our business. In addition, we may be subject to significant liability should the consumption of any of our products cause injury, illness or death.
Pending and future litigation may lead us to incur significant costs.
We face risks associated with our defined benefit pension plan.
We generate agricultural food packaging wastes and are subject to substantial environmental regulation.

Our production capacity for certain products and commodities is concentrated in a limited number of facilities, exposing us to a material disruption in production in the event that a disaster strikes.
We may undertake acquisitions or product innovations and may have difficulties integrating them or may not realize the anticipated benefits.
We are dependent upon a seasonal workforce and our inability to hire sufficient employees may adversely affect our business.
Increases in labor costs or work stoppages or strikes could materially and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
There may be increased governmental legislative and regulatory activity in reaction to consumer perception related to enamels.
The implementation of the Food Safety Modernization Act of 2011 may affect operations.
Our results are dependent on successful marketplace initiatives and acceptance by consumers of our products.
Financing Risks
Global economic conditions may materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our ability to manage our working capital and our Revolving Credit Facility is critical to our success.
Failure to comply with the requirements of our debt agreements could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Risks Relating to Our Stock
Our existing shareholders, if acting together, may be able to exert control over matters requiring shareholder approval.
Our certificate of incorporation and bylaws contain provisions that discourage corporate takeovers.
We have not paid dividends on our common stock in the past.
Tax legislation could impact future cash flows.
The tax status of our insurance subsidiary could be challenged resulting in an acceleration of income tax payments.
paragraphs: The following factors as well as factors described elsewhere in this Form 10-K or in other filings by the Company with the SEC, could adversely affect the Company's consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows. Other factors not presently known to us or that we presently believe are not material could also affect our business operations or financial results. The Company refers to itself as "we", "our" or "us" in this section.

If canned vegetable, frozen vegetable, or jarred fruit categories decline, less shelf space will be devoted to these categories in the supermarkets. Fresh and perishable businesses are improving their delivery systems around the world and the availability of fresh produce is impacting the consumer purchasing patterns relating to packaged fruit and vegetables. Our financial performance and growth are related to conditions in the United States' fruit and vegetable packaging industry which is a mature industry. Our net sales are a function of product availability and market pricing. In the fruit and vegetable packaging industry, product availability and market prices tend to have an inverse relationship: market prices tend to decrease as more product is available and to increase if less product is available. Product availability is a direct result of plantings, growing conditions, crop yields and inventory levels, all of which vary from year to year. These factors may have a significant effect on supply and competition and create downward pressure on prices. In addition, market prices can be affected by the planting and inventory levels and individual pricing decisions of our competitors. Generally, market prices in the fruit and vegetable packaging industry adjust more quickly to variations in product availability than an individual packager can adjust its cost structure; thus, in an oversupply situation, a packager's margins likely will weaken. We typically have experienced lower margins during times of industry oversupply.

In the past, the fruit and vegetable packaging industry has been characterized by excess capacity, with resulting pressure on our prices and profit margins. We have closed packaging plants in past years in response to the downward pressure on prices. There can be no assurance that our margins will improve in response to favorable market conditions or that we will be able to operate profitably during depressed market conditions.

Our operations are affected by the growing cycles of the vegetables we package. When the vegetables are ready to be picked, we must harvest and package them quickly or lose the opportunity to package the impacted vegetables for an entire year. Most of our vegetables are grown by farmers under contract with us. Consequently, we must pay the contract grower for the vegetables even if we cannot or do not harvest or package them. Most of our production occurs during the second quarter (July through September) of our fiscal year, which corresponds with the quarter that the majority of the produce is harvested and subsequently packaged.

A majority of our sales occur during the second and third quarters of each fiscal year due to seasonal consumption patterns for our products. Accordingly, inventory levels and accounts receivable levels are generally highest during the second and third quarters. Net sales generated during our second and third fiscal quarters have a significant impact on our results of operations. Because of these seasonal fluctuations, the results of any particular quarter, particularly in the first half of our fiscal year, will not necessarily be indicative of results for the full year or for future years.

We set our planting schedules without knowing the effect of the weather on the crops or on the entire industry's production. Weather conditions during the course of each vegetable crop's growing season will affect the volume and growing time of that crop. As most of our vegetables are produced in more than one part of the United States, this somewhat reduces the risk that our entire crop will be subject to disastrous weather. The upper Midwest is the primary growing region for the principal vegetables which we pack, namely peas, green beans and sweet corn, and it is also a substantial source of our competitors' vegetable production. A sizeable portion of our vegetable production areas are located in well-draining soils and are also serviced by irrigation systems to help minimize dry conditions during the growing season. Any adverse effects of weather-related reduced production may be partially mitigated by higher selling prices for the vegetables which are produced.

paragraphs: Seneca Foods Corporation ("Seneca" or the "Company") 於 1949 年成立，並透過內部成長與戰略收購，發展成為美國首屈一指的包裝水果與蔬菜供應商，擁有 27 個主要設施，分佈於美國各地。這些設施包含包裝廠、罐頭製造廠、種子生產廠、農場運作及物流支援網路。食品包裝運作主要由紐約、密歇根、俄勒岡、威斯康辛、華盛頓、愛達荷、伊利諾、明尼蘇達及亞利桑那州的廠區支援。本公司亦維護倉庫，通常位於其包裝廠附近。本公司於紐約州註冊，總部位於紐約州法爾波特 350 WillowBrook Office Park，郵遞區號 14450，電話號碼為 (585) 495-4100。
本公司的業務策略旨在擴大市佔率並提升銷售與毛利率。這些策略包括：1) 增強本公司在包裝水果與蔬菜產業的領導地位；2) 透過消除本公司供應鏈的成本與投資最先進的生產與物流科技，提供低成本、高品質的水果與蔬菜產品給消費者；3) 投資成長機會；以及 4) 跟進戰略收購，以發揮本公司核心競爭優勢。

本公司的網站網址為 www.senecafoods.com。本公司依照 1934 年證券交易法第 13(a) 或 15(d) 節規定，所提交的年度報告表 10-K、季報表 10-Q、現況報告表 8-K 以及任何對這些報告的更正或補充文件，皆可在本公司網站上取得，於這些文件電子提交至或提供給 SEC 後盡速公開。本公司網站上所有這些申報文件皆可免費取得。本公司網站上的資訊並非年度報告表 10-K 的一部分。
此外，本公司網站包含與公司治理相關的資訊，包括董事會各委員會的章程以及本公司商業行為準則與倫理規範。本公司有意在其網站上公開任何對商業行為準則與倫理規範的修正或豁免，若這些修正或豁免需依照 SEC 與 NASDAQ 的規則進行公開披露。

本公司幾乎完全根據兩個應報告分部來管理其業務：蔬菜與水果/零食。其他類別包含非食品業務，包括來自罐頭、罐頭蓋、種子銷售以及本公司飛機業務的外部收入，以及某些公司層面的項目。在財務年度 2026 年，本公司收購了 Green Giant 美國速凍業務，該業務屬於蔬菜應報告分部。此收購增強了本公司現有的速凍能力，並擴大其在速凍類別的影響力。有關更多細節，請參閱 Part II, Item 8, "財務報表與補充資料" 中的 Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements 第 16 註的 "收購" 項目。

本公司食品業務在財務年度 2026 年佔總淨銷售額的 98%。罐頭蔬菜佔 82%，凍結蔬菜佔 9%，水果產品佔 6%，零食產品佔 1% 的總食品包裝淨銷售額。非食品包裝銷售佔本公司財務年度 2026 年淨銷售額的 2%。有關更多討論，請參閱 Part II, Item 8, "財務報表與補充資料" 中的 Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements 第 13 註的 "分部資訊" 項目。

headings: 水果與蔬菜產業風險
水果與蔬菜產業過度的生產能力會對銷售價格產生向下壓力。
生長週期及惡劣天氣條件可能降低我們的營運結果。
我們所包裝或需要的原材料等大宗商品，可能因價格上漲而對我們的獲利能力產生不利影響。
與我們營運相關的風險
經濟條件的變化影響消費者支出，可能對我們的業務造成損害。
我們依賴關鍵客戶。
若我們無法維持產品的市場佔有率，將可能對我們的業務與營收產生不利影響。
物流及其他運輸相關成本的增加可能對我們的營運成果造成重大不利影響。
我們產品的召回可能對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。此外，若我們的產品被使用後導致傷害、疾病或死亡，我們可能面臨重大賠償責任。
未解決及未來的法律訴訟可能導致我們產生重大成本。
我們面臨與確定福利退休金計畫相關的風險。
我們產生農業食品包裝廢棄物，並受重大環境法規管制。
我們某些產品及商品的生產能力集中於有限數量的廠區，若發生災難，可能導致生產重大中斷。
我們可能進行收購或產品創新，但可能在整合這些業務時遇到困難，或無法實現預期的效益。
我們依賴季節性勞工，若無法聘足員工，可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
勞動成本增加或工會罷工等情況，可能對本公司的財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
因消費者對搪瓷產品的觀感，政府可能增加相關立法與監管活動。
2011 年食品安全現代化法案的實施，可能影響本公司的營運。
本公司營運成果依賴市場推廣計畫的成功執行及消費者對本公司產品的接受度。
融資風險
總體經濟狀況可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司管理營運資金及週轉信用融資能力，是本公司成功關鍵。
未能遵守本公司債務協議的相關要求，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
與本公司股票相關的風險
本公司現有股東，若共同行動，可能能控制需股東批准的事項。
本公司章程及章程規則包含條款，可能阻卻公司收購。
本公司過去未曾就普通股發放股息。
稅製法規可能影響未來現金流量。
本公司保險子公司之稅務地位可能遭質疑，導致所得稅款加速支付。
paragraphs: 以下因素以及本表10-K或其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的文件中所描述的其他因素，可能會對本公司的合併財務狀況、營運結果或現金流量產生不利影響。其他目前尚未為我們所知或目前認為不具重大影響的因素，也可能影響我們的業務營運或財務結果。本公司在本節中將自己稱為「我們」、「我們的」或「我們」。

如果罐頭蔬菜、凍結蔬菜或罐裝水果類別衰退，超級市場將會減少這些類別的展示空間。新鮮與易腐商品的業務正在全球改善其配送系統，新鮮農產品的可得性正在影響消費者對包裝水果和蔬菜的購買模式。我們的財務表現與成長與美國水果和蔬菜包裝產業的狀況有關，而該產業屬於成熟產業。我們的淨銷售額取決於產品可得性與市場價格。在水果和蔬菜包裝產業中，產品可得性與市場價格通常呈現反向關係：市場價格會隨著更多產品可得而下降，若產品較少則會上升。產品可得性直接取決於種植、成長條件、收成量與存貨水準，這些因素每年皆可能有所不同。這些因素可能對供應與競爭產生重大影響，並對價格造成下行壓力。此外，市場價格也可能受到競爭對手的種植與存貨水準以及個別價格決策的影響。通常而言，水果和蔬菜包裝產業的市場價格會比個別包裝商調整其成本結構的速度更快反應產品可得性的變動；因此，在供過於求的情況下，包裝商的毛利率很可能會下降。我們通常在產業供過於求時經歷較低的毛利率。
過去，水果和蔬菜包裝產業特徵為過度生產能力，導致我們的價格與利潤率受到壓力。我們在過去幾年已關閉一些包裝廠以回應價格下跌的壓力。無法保證我們的毛利率會因有利的市場條件而改善，或是在市場低迷時我們能夠維持獲利。
我們的營運受到我們包裝的蔬菜種植週期的影響。當蔬菜成熟準備採收時，我們必須迅速採收與包裝，否則將失去整年包裝這些蔬菜的機會。我們大部分的蔬菜是由與我們簽約的農民種植的。因此，即使我們無法或不採收與包裝這些蔬菜，我們仍必須支付給簽約農民。我們大部分的生產發生在財務年度的第二季（7月至9月），這與大多數農產品收穫並隨後包裝的季節相符。
我們大部分的銷售發生在每個財務年度的第二與第三季，這是因為我們產品的季節性消費模式。因此，存貨水準與應收帳款水準通常在第二與第三季達到最高。我們在第二與第三財務季所產生的淨銷售額對我們的營運結果有重大影響。由於這些季節性波動，任何特定季度的結果，特別是在財務年度的前半段，不一定能代表全年或未來年度的結果。

我們在設定種植排程時，並不知道天氣對作物或整個產業生產的影響。在每種蔬菜的生長季節中，天氣條件會影響該作物的產量與生長時間。由於我們大部分的蔬菜是在美國多個地區生產的，這在一定程度上減少了我們整體作物遭受災害性天氣的風險。美國上中西部地區是我們包裝的主要蔬菜（即豌豆、青豆與甜玉米）的主要種植區，同時也是我們競爭對手蔬菜生產的重要來源。我們的蔬菜生產區域中，有相當大的一部分位於排水良好的土壤上，並配有灌溉系統，以幫助在生長季節中減少乾旱條件的影響。任何與天氣相關的生產減少的不利影響，可能透過這些蔬菜的銷售價格提高而部分緩解。
